open_failures.detail: No venue given by TASK.md and none implied by the evidence.
open_failures.resolution: generic profile adopted, all rules marked assumed:true; logged in open_issues.md

accepted_risks.decision: project/ contains only the extracted paper text and the README -- no results/ or notes/ directory, so there is no separate machine-written log layer that evidence_model.md's hard/soft split assumes. Decision: values the paper presents as the outcome of a stated, specific measurement or definition (Table 1 quality targets, Sec 4.1-4.4 measured accuracies/AUCs, Sec 5.3 protocol, Sec 5.2 division rules, Table 2 submission facts) are logged strength='hard' with locator=project/paper.txt, since paper.txt is this run's sole authoritative data layer of record. The authors' own qualitative/interpretive prose (Insights paragraphs, impact/risk remarks) is logged strength='soft'. No accuracy/AUC figure has repeated-run variance reported by the source, so those specific items are additionally marked status='incomplete' and their derived claims carry confidence <= moderate.

Table 2's extraction merges/drops some cells (see missing_evidence.json MISS-004). The open-division row's Dataset mark was reconstructed from an explicit, independently-stated fact elsewhere in the same paper (Sec 6.2: no submission changed the dataset) rather than invented; Training/Model are inferred as modified from the use of quantization-aware training (QKeras), which the closed-division rule forbids. Flagged to the reader in the claim map (L003) and in the paper's own table note rather than presented as a clean read.

[19] (Torelli and Bangale, MLMark whitepaper) is load-bearing for the Related Work gap and is cited as '(Torelli and Bangale, n.d.)' rather than inventing a year. [1] (TinyML Foundation) and [16] (Moreau/Edge Impulse) are not given inline citations; their content is either paraphrased without attribution ([1], a field name) or dropped from the main text ([16]).

Literature mode is limited to the 22 works already cited in project/paper.txt's own reference list, registered with verification.method='user_supplied_file' and read_depth='abstract'. No snowballing, no independent verification of metadata beyond what the reference-list entry itself states, no retraction check possible.
No venue specified; generic fallback profile used per templates/venue_profile.generic.yaml, all rules marked assumed:true.

accepted_risks.topic: source_registry.json schema vs. an undated source
accepted_risks.decision: schemas/source_registry.schema.json requires 'year' to be a plain integer (no null allowed), but SRC-019 (Torelli and Bangale, MLMark whitepaper) has no year anywhere in project/paper.txt's reference list. Hard Rule 1 ('never invent... numbers') outranks strict schema conformance, so SRC-019.year is left null and the source is still cited in the paper as '(Torelli and Bangale, n.d.)'. tools/validate_artifacts.py therefore reports exactly one ERROR ($.sources[15].year: expected type ['integer'], got NoneType); this is a known, accepted, documented exception, not an unnoticed failure.

schemas/source_registry.schema.json requires a 'level' enum (1-4) but no doc defining its meaning exists in this trimmed skill copy (docs/02_RESEARCH_CORPUS_STRATEGY.md is referenced by workflow.md/corpus_agent.md but not present under ./rce). Adopted rubric, recorded here for auditability: 1 = peer-reviewed venue explicitly named (conference proceedings/journal), 2 = arXiv/CoRR preprint, 3 = institutional technical report or dataset/benchmark webpage without stated peer review, 4 = blog/opinion/commentary (unused; none of the 19 registered sources are this).
